hook: The country with the most meat per person isn't America. It's Tonga.
twist: In FAO's 2023 food balances Tonga has 157 kg of meat per person a year, ahead of Mongolia (136) and the Marshall Islands (126); the US is fourth (122). India has 8 kg.
angle: Countdown 4 to 1 from one FAO dataset (via Our World in Data), then the other end of the table. One big number: 157 kg.
why_now: Demand: the 2026-10-06 scout's food-per-country cluster: 'Most vs Least Oil-Using Countries' 26.8M on a 61k-sub channel (outlier 439), 'Which Country Eats The Most Meat' 9.5M (119k subs), 'Which Country Eats The Most Chicken' 8.3M; YouTube search 'which country eats the most meat' (2026-10-07): median of top 25 7.2M. Data: FAO food balances for 2023, published through Our World in Data.
risks: FAO measures meat supply (available for consumption, incl. waste), not meat eaten: label 'meat supply per person' on screen.
Small island states: Tonga's figure rests on imports; avoid any judgement of diets or bodies.
